description: Group Evolving Agents: Open-Ended Self-Improvement via Experience Sharing

summary.one_liner: Research code for Group Evolving Agents (GEA), a method where a group of coding agents is the evolutionary unit and agents share experience with each other during open-ended self-improvement.
summary.what_it_does: The repository implements the Group Evolving Agents algorithm, where a group of agents rather than a single agent is treated as the unit of evolution, with experience shared and reused within the group across generations. The entry point is GEA_outer.py, and the initial coding agent is defined in coding_agent.py. Foundation model prompts and tools live in prompts/ and tools/. Evaluation is run on SWE-bench (a clone of the SWE-bench repo at a pinned commit is required) and on the Polyglot benchmark, which is prepared via a provided module. The README also includes analysis scripts for plotting and graphs, and it ships logs and performance records for the initial agent on both benchmarks. The codebase is stated to build on the Darwin Gödel Machine code.
use_cases: Reproducing the Group Evolving Agents experiments
Running self-improving coding agent evolution on SWE-bench
Evaluating evolved agents on the Polyglot benchmark
Studying open-ended agent evolution and experience sharing
Plotting and analyzing agent evolution results
how_to_run: Export OPENAI_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in your shell profile
Verify Docker works with `docker run hello-world` (add user to docker group if needed)
python3 -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt
Clone SWE-bench into swe_bench/, checkout commit dc4c087c2b9e4cefebf2e3d201d27e36, and run pip install -e .
Prepare the Polyglot dataset with `python -m polyglot.prepare_polyglot_dataset`
notable: Treats a group of agents as the evolutionary unit, with explicit experience sharing and reuse inside the group
Built on the Darwin Gödel Machine (DGM) codebase, as acknowledged in the README
Evaluates on both SWE-bench and the Polyglot benchmark
Ships logs and performance records for the initial agent on both benchmarks
caveats: Requires paid API keys for OpenAI and Anthropic models
Requires Docker to be installed and configured, and the setup involves several manual steps
The README's SWE-bench clone command has no repository URL filled in, so the setup step is incomplete as written
Analysis scripts need extra system packages (graphviz) and a separate requirements_dev.txt
